conclusion.label: endorses

report:
### Conclusion
Whole-body vibration (WBV) therapy is effective as a safe, complementary strategy to help lower fracture risk and mitigate bone loss in individuals with osteoporosis. Research demonstrates that mechanical stress stimulation from WBV improves bone mineral density (BMD)—particularly in the lumbar spine and hip regions—and helps reduce fall rates among older adults. While WBV is a valuable non-invasive physical therapy, clinical evidence supports its role primarily as a supplementary intervention alongside standard lifestyle and pharmacological management, rather than a standalone replacement.

### Research Summary
* **Bone Mineral Density Maintenance:** Mechanical stimulation from WBV helps regulate bone metabolism and reduces bone loss in postmenopausal women, specifically demonstrating positive effects in the lumbar spine and hip (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/endocrinology/articles/10.3389/fendo.2025.1611677/full; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13018-016-0357-2).
* **Fall and Fracture Prevention:** Systematic reviews and meta-analyses indicate that WBV exercise reduces both fall rates and fracture risk in adults aged 50 and older, serving as an accessible exercise alternative for individuals unable to perform high-impact training (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6027066/; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0965229922000139).
